chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-A'ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'Arrogance (al-kibr) may be found in the worst of people from every race, and arrogance is the Gown of Allah. So whoever disputes with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for His Gown, Allah will not increase him except in lowliness.'

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) passed by one of the streets of Medina, and Sawda was gathering manure. It was said to her, 'Move aside from the way of the Messenger of Allah!' So she said, 'The road is open (wide enough).' Then some of the people thought of grabbing her, so the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Leave her, for she is tyrannical (bully).'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of arrogance being the 'Gown of Allah' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates arrogance (kibr) as a divine attribute by describing it as Allah's 'Gown' (rida'), warning that those who compete with Him for it are relegated to lowliness. It illustrates this through the narrative of Sawda, a woman of strong will who refused to yield the path to the Prophet, demonstrating that such dominant character can exist even among ordinary people. This narrative highlights the distinction between physical strength or stubbornness and the spiritual vice of disputing with the Divine.
